PO Box 10341  
Van Nuys, CA 91410  

Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination  
Member: Rowan Ellison  
Member ID: W486282210  
Plan: Ambetter of North Carolina  
Reference number: POC-5D5B151DE3-65694  
Requested service: ACL reconstruction  
CPT: 29888  

Dear Grievances and Appeals Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888. The denial states that the submitted clinical records did not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery.

The records do document extensive conservative treatment:

- I have had 14 months of progressive knee pain that has not improved with rest.
- I used NSAIDs for eight months, with inadequate relief.
- I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy from March 27, 2026, through July 3, 2026. The treatment included range-of-motion work, quadriceps strengthening, and bracing. The physical therapy discharge note documents completion of 20 visits.
- I received a corticosteroid injection on May 28, 2026. It provided only two weeks of partial relief.
- Despite these measures, I continue to experience recurrent instability with pivoting and have had two episodes of giving way on stairs.

The clinical findings also establish a significant structural injury and ongoing functional impairment. The July 1, 2026 MRI shows a complete midsubstance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with a bone-bruise pattern. The menisci are intact, and there is no significant arthritis. Examination shows positive provocative testing on the affected side, and range of motion is limited by pain. Dr. Okafor, an orthopedic surgeon, has requested ACL reconstruction based on these findings and the failure of conservative care.

The record therefore addresses the stated basis for denial. Conservative treatment was not brief or incomplete: it included months of medication, supervised physical therapy with bracing and strengthening, and an injection, without adequate relief. Continued instability despite this treatment presents an ongoing safety and functional concern.

I also have no documented active infection or untreated substance use. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker. These records do not identify a separate medical reason that would prevent the requested surgery.

I request that Ambetter overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for ACL reconstruction, CPT 29888. Please have the appeal reviewed using the complete clinical record, including the physical therapy discharge note, medication history, injection response, MRI report, examination findings, and orthopedic surgical recommendation.

The plan has not provided a publicly available policy document specific to CPT 29888 that I can quote. Ambetter’s public clinical-policy information indicates that InterQual criteria may be used when no applicable Ambetter clinical policy exists. If InterQual or other clinical-review criteria were applied to this request, please provide the exact criteria used, including the applicable version or date, and identify any specific requirement that Ambetter believes remains unsatisfied.

Please acknowledge receipt of this appeal and send the appeal determination in writing. This appeal is being submitted within the stated 180-day appeal period, no later than February 13, 2027.

Sincerely,

Rowan Ellison
